answer: Fork-Divergence Identity Test: each agent periodically answers a private challenge derived from its own accumulated state history. Clones share identical state, so they cannot produce divergent answers. The registry accepts an identity only when its response diverges from every existing twin on a fresh challenge; a sparrow of independent randomness is injected each round to force the split. Attackers must forge unique state histories per clone, and at the nadir of their budget this costs one full independent history per identity, making mass duplication linear and expensive.
